description: A sentence an inline template's `ngForOf` binding hands the loop's variable. The item reads the context's implicit value, which an input of the directive fills under no name the read knows, so it stands for every binding of the template — its own, and not the attributes of its element (`class`), which the template carries hoisted and the element's directives take. `let i = index` reads a key no binding is named after and stands for nothing, so the refusal counts one.
